messages.content: You check claims about a scientific paper against the evidence each one cites. A claim is supported only if the cited evidence says it AS WRITTEN: the same subject, row, column, setting and number. A correct value attached to the wrong subject or row is NOT supported, and neither is a claim that goes beyond its evidence. Judge only from the cited evidence; figure images are attached where a claim cites a figure. Give a verdict for every claim.

Claims:
1. "The AMR-to-parse model performs better than the Text-to-parse model in terms of unlabelled F1 score, with a score of 60.4 compared to 87.5 for the Text-to-parse model." -- cites: E5 (Section Table 1): quote "AMR-to-parse 60.4 54.8"; E5 (Section Table 1): quote "Text-to-parse 87.5 85.8"
2. "The AMR-to-parse model performs worse than the Text-to-parse model in terms of labelled F1 score, with a score of 54.8 compared to 85.8 for the Text-to-parse model." -- cites: E5 (Section Table 1): quote "AMR-to-parse 60.4 54.8"; E5 (Section Table 1): quote "Text-to-parse 87.5 85.8"
3. "The baseline model, which is the unconditional LSTM, performs with an unlabelled F1 score of 38.5." -- cites: E5 (Section Table 1): quote "Unconditional 38.5 31.7"

Cited evidence:
[E5] (text, Section Table 1, page 4): Table 1: Parsing scores on LDC2017T10 dev set. Model Unlabelled F1 Labelled F1 Text-to-parse 87.5 85.8 AMR-to-parse 60.4 54.8 Unconditional 38.5 31.7

verdicts.reason: The claim states that the AMR-to-parse model has a score of 60.4 in terms of unlabelled F1 score, which is incorrect. The evidence shows that the AMR-to-parse model has a score of 60.4 in terms of labelled F1 score, not unlabelled F1 score.
The evidence shows that the AMR-to-parse model has a score of 54.8 in terms of labelled F1 score, which is lower than the score of 85.8 for the Text-to-parse model.
The evidence shows that the baseline model, which is the unconditional LSTM, has an unlabelled F1 score of 38.5.
